catalog: Prepares working professionals to manage the people side of organizational performance. Students learn to diagnose why employees and teams underperform, deliver feedback that actually changes behavior, build and repair team dynamics, delegate and make decision-rights calls under pressure, lead a team through change, and hire well. 3 credit hours.
vision: MGMT 615 sits at the center of the Flex Online people-management sequence: the course that turns someone who's good at their job into someone who's good at running a team. Other Flex Online courses build a student's functional expertise; this one builds the management judgment that lets them use it, on a team, under real conditions. What sets it apart is a diagnosis-first approach: instead of handing students a checklist of leadership techniques, every module makes them figure out what's actually wrong before choosing a fix, then defend that call to their peers in a live cohort session or a mock interview panel. By the end, students can run the conversations that actually move a career forward: a feedback conversation that changes behavior, a delegation call made under pressure, a change announcement that survives contact with a skeptical team, a structured hire instead of a gut-feel one. These are the skills that separate someone ready to manage a bigger team from someone who's simply good at running the current one. Mastery here means producing the script, the memo, or the scorecard a student would actually use at work.
clos: CLO 1: Apply core theories of motivation and performance to diagnose why an employee or team is underperforming.
CLO 2: Design a feedback or coaching conversation that changes an employee's behavior, not just documents it.
CLO 3: Evaluate team dynamics and organizational context to select a management intervention appropriate to the actual problem.
CLO 4: Make a delegation or decision-rights call and justify the trade-offs involved.
CLO 5: Communicate a management decision in language a direct report can act on immediately.
